Harrisburg & the West Shore 30

Midtown, Camp Hill, Mechanicsburg

  1. Must see · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Pennsylvania State Capitol

    Joseph Huston's 1906 Beaux-Arts capitol, its dome modeled on St. Peter's — Theodore Roosevelt called it the handsomest he'd seen. Moravian tile floors by Henry Mercer, Violet Oakley and Edwin Austin Abbey murals; free 30-minute guided tours every half hour on weekdays.

    Look for ICON

    501 N 3rd St, Harrisburg, PA 17120

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg, Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney)

  2. Must see · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    National Civil War Museum

    Hilltop museum in Reservoir Park that tells the whole war — causes, both armies, the home front and aftermath — evenhandedly, without picking sides; one of the largest Civil War collections in the country.

    Look for MUS

    1 Lincoln Cir, Harrisburg, PA 17103

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit PA (state tourism office), Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB)

  3. Must see · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Walnut Street Bridge & City Island

    The 1890 'People's Bridge,' a wrought-iron truss now open only to walkers and cyclists, carries you from Riverfront Park across the Susquehanna to City Island — home of the Senators' ballpark, a riverboat, beach and the best skyline view of the Capitol dome.

    Look for PARK

    Walnut St at Front St, Harrisburg, PA 17101

    Recommended by Wikipedia, City of Harrisburg (official), Susquehanna Greenway Partnership

  4. Must see · American & New American · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    The Millworks

    Midtown Harrisburg's 'Art. Food. Music.' hub since 2015, built from the reclaimed timber of the old Stokes Millwork: a farm-to-table restaurant, brewery and rooftop biergarten over two floors of working artist studios. Named to OpenTable's Top 100 Hot Spot Restaurants in America. Order: Farm-to-table plates and house-brewed beer in the rooftop biergarten.

    340 Verbeke St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by Visit Hershey & Harrisburg, PA Eats, Central Penn Business Journal

  5. Must see · Coffee & Cafés · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Little Amps Coffee Roasters

    Harrisburg's home-grown roaster (2010, founded by a rock drummer) — Uptown flagship plus downtown State St and Strawberry Square outposts; its barista won a national best-espresso contest. Order: House-roasted espresso (Best Espresso in America contest winner, 2018).

    1836 Green St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by PA Eats, TheBurg (Harrisburg civic magazine), FOX43 WPMT (York)

  6. Must see · Bakeries, Shoofly & Whoopie Pies · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Raising the Bar Bakery

    Scratch bakery that grew up inside the Broad Street Market and now bakes croissants and breads in Midtown's old Carpets and Draperies building. Order: Seasonal croissants, rustic breads and dessert bars.

    1507 N 3rd St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by TheBurg (Harrisburg civic magazine), PA Eats, Visit PA (state tourism office)

  7. Must see · American & New American · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Isabelle's Southern Cuisine

    Kim Ross's Midtown soul-food restaurant cooking her grandmother Isabelle's recipes — Visit PA's pick for Harrisburg Sunday brunch. Order: Isabelle's chicken & waffles, fried fish & grits.

    306 Reily St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by TheBurg (Harrisburg civic magazine), Visit PA (state tourism office), Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  8. Must see · Markets · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Broad Street Market

    Founded in 1860 (it fed Union soldiers at Camp Curtin) and among the oldest continuously operating market houses in the US; on the National Register since 1974. Midtown Harrisburg's anchor, run by the non-profit Broad Street Market Alliance. Thu–Sat only. Order: Pennsylvania Dutch stands alongside the city's international food counters — eat your way through both brick and stone market houses.

    1233 N 3rd St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by Historic Harrisburg Association, Clio (Marshall University)

  9. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Pizza Boy Brewing Co.

    West Shore brewery grown out of Al's of Hampden pizza shop — industrial setting, but routinely named the region's best beer, with around 100 drafts. Order: Barrel-aged and one-off beers from 100-ish taps, with pies from Al's of Hampden.

    2240 Millennium Way, Enola, PA 17025

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), PA Eats

  10. Must see · American & New American · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    The Jackson House

    Midtown burger counter making what FOX43 calls arguably the city's best burger and cheesesteak since 1982 — a Visit Hershey & Harrisburg 'uniquely Harrisburg' pick. Order: Charbroiled half-pound burger with house Jackson Sauce; cheesesteaks.

    1004 N 6th St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by FOX43 WPMT (York), Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  11. Worth the detour · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    State Museum of Pennsylvania

    The Commonwealth's own museum beside the Capitol, run by the PA Historical and Museum Commission: four floors from mastodons and Native Pennsylvania to Peter Rothermel's huge 'Battle of Gettysburg: Pickett's Charge' painting, plus a 70-seat digital planetarium.

    Look for MUS

    300 North St, Harrisburg, PA 17120

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), Clio (Marshall University)

  12. Worth the detour · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Fort Hunter Mansion and Park

    A Federal-style stone mansion (1814) on the site of a French and Indian War fort, in a 40-acre Dauphin County riverside park with a covered bridge, gardens and a tavern museum six miles up the Susquehanna from downtown.

    Look for HIST

    5300 N Front St, Harrisburg, PA 17110

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Susquehanna Greenway Partnership, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  13. Worth the detour · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Rockville Bridge

    The longest stone-masonry arch railroad viaduct ever built: 48 arches and 3,820 feet across the Susquehanna, completed by the Pennsylvania Railroad in 1902 and still carrying Norfolk Southern freights and Amtrak's Pennsylvanian. Best seen from the Marysville or Fort Hunter river banks.

    Look for RAIL

    Susquehanna River between Rockville and Marysville, PA

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Asce, Railfan Guides

  14. Worth the detour · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    John Harris–Simon Cameron Mansion

    Built in 1766 by city founder John Harris Jr. and later the home of Lincoln's first Secretary of War, Simon Cameron — one of Harrisburg's oldest buildings and a National Historic Landmark, run as a museum by the Historical Society of Dauphin County.

    Look for HIST

    219 S Front St, Harrisburg, PA 17104

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Historical Society of Dauphin County, National Park Service

  15. Worth the detour · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Dauphin Narrows Statue of Liberty

    A 25-foot Lady Liberty on a river piling — a 1986 patriotic prank, blown down in 1992 and replaced in metal by helicopter in 1997.

    Look for ODD

    Susquehanna River, Dauphin Narrows (visible from US-22/322), Dauphin, PA 17018

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg, Visit PA (state tourism office)

  16. Worth the detour · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Pennsylvania Farm Show Complex

    24-acre home of the nation's largest indoor agricultural exposition each January — half a million visitors, a butter sculpture and 20,000 Dairymen's milkshakes a day.

    Look for ICON

    2300 N Cameron St, Harrisburg, PA 17110

    Recommended by Visit Hershey & Harrisburg, Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), Visit PA (state tourism office)

  17. Worth the detour · Italian & Pizza · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Alvaro Bread and Pastry Shoppe

    Midtown Italian bakery run since 2005 by Sal and Lina Alvaro, immigrants from Italy — FOX43's pick for the area's best Italian food. Order: Cannoli, sfogliatelle, Italian breads and lunch plates.

    236 Peffer St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by FOX43 WPMT (York), Visit Hershey & Harrisburg, TheBurg (Harrisburg civic magazine)

  18. Worth the detour · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Susquehanna Art Museum

    Midtown's contemporary art museum, opened in its purpose-built home (wrapped around a 1916 bank vault) in 2015, with rotating exhibitions — steps from Broad Street Market.

    Look for MUS

    1401 N 3rd St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  19. Worth the detour · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Whitaker Center for Science and the Arts

    Downtown Harrisburg's science center, Sunoco Performance Theater and digital cinema under one roof — the region's go-to hands-on museum for families.

    Look for FAM

    222 Market St, Harrisburg, PA 17101

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  20. Worth the detour · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Riverfront Park & Holocaust Memorial

    Harrisburg's 1912 City Beautiful riverfront — miles of Susquehanna promenade, steps and gardens along Front Street — named one of America's Great Public Spaces by the American Planning Association; the Holocaust Memorial for the Commonwealth (1994) stands at Sayford Street.

    Look for PARK

    Front St & Sayford St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Apa

  21. Worth the detour · American & New American · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    1700 Degrees Steakhouse

    Downtown steakhouse in the Hilton Harrisburg, named the best steakhouse in Pennsylvania by Mashed (2025), weighing reviews, accolades and recommendations. Order: New York strip and truffle-lobster mac 'n' cheese.

    1 N 2nd St (Hilton Harrisburg), Harrisburg, PA 17101

    Recommended by Mashed, abc27 WHTM (Harrisburg)

  22. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Ever Grain Brewing Co.

    Camp Hill warehouse brewery (2016) known for hazy IPAs and stouts, board games and a window into the kitchen next door. Order: Joose juicy IPA and Dark Necessity imperial stout.

    4444 Carlisle Pike, Camp Hill, PA 17011

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), TheBurg (Harrisburg civic magazine)

  23. Worth the detour · Coffee & Cafés · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Elementary Coffee Co.

    Andrea Grove-Musselman's roaster, born at the Broad Street Market in 2014, now a café in a renovated Capitol-district building (and back at the market after the 2023 fire). Order: Small-batch roasts sweetened only with natural sweeteners and spices.

    256 North St, Harrisburg, PA 17101

    Recommended by TheBurg (Harrisburg civic magazine), PA Eats

  24. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Note Bistro & Wine Bar

    Midtown neighbourhood bistro in a repurposed 1910 Victorian home, with sidewalk tables on Second Street. Order: European-inspired bistro plates and an Old World wine list.

    1530 N 2nd St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by PA Eats, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  25. Worth the detour · American & New American · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Valley Bistro

    West Shore bistro that has won Cumberland Valley's Meal Madness bracket twice and was a 2026 reader-vote finalist for best breakfast/brunch. Order: Brunch and bistro plates.

    4520 Valley Rd, Enola, PA 17025

    Recommended by Visit Cumberland Valley, The Sentinel (Carlisle) / cumberlink.com

  26. Worth the detour · American & New American · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Greystone Public House

    Colonial Park gastropub in a historic stone building, recommended by PA Eats and the Hershey–Harrisburg visitor bureau. Order: Gastropub plates and craft beer in a stone building.

    2120 Colonial Rd, Harrisburg, PA 17112

    Recommended by PA Eats, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  27. Worth the detour · American & New American · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    The Watershed Pub

    First pub in Camp Hill since Prohibition (The Sentinel), in a renovated 1830s building with a wraparound front porch. Order: Pub fare and local drafts on the wraparound porch.

    2129 Market St, Camp Hill, PA 17011

    Recommended by The Sentinel (Carlisle) / cumberlink.com, Visit Cumberland Valley

    Pennsylvania Governor's Residence

    The governor's riverfront home — free guided tours Tue/Thu in spring and fall, self-guided in December, and a fixture of the Candlelight House Tour since 1980.

    Look for HIST

    2035 N Front St, Harrisburg, PA 17102

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), TheBurg (Harrisburg civic magazine), Witf (Harrisburg public media — NPR/PBS)

    Wildwood Park

    90 acres of trails, wetlands and a free nature center around Wildwood Lake, inside the city limits.

    100 Wildwood Way, Harrisburg, PA 17110

  30. Deep cut · Italian & Pizza · Harrisburg & the West Shore

    Bacco Pizzeria & Wine Bar

Hershey & Derry Township 20

Hummelstown, Middletown, Palmyra

  1. Must see · Hershey & Derry Township

    The Hershey Story

    The museum of Milton Hershey's town and company on Chocolate Avenue (opened 2009) — and its Chocolate Lab, where you temper, pour and decorate your own bar; the tasting of world drinking chocolates is the sleeper hit.

    Look for MUS

    63 W Chocolate Ave, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg, Central Penn Business Journal

  2. Must see · Hershey & Derry Township

    Indian Echo Caverns

    Show cave on the Swatara Creek bluff between Hershey and Hummelstown, open to visitors since 1929; the 45-minute tour passes the Indian Ballroom and tells of William Wilson, the 'Pennsylvania Hermit' who lived here for 19 years.

    Look for FAM

    368 Middletown Rd, Hummelstown, PA 17036

    Recommended by Wikipedia, PA Bucket List, Roadside America

  3. Must see · Diners & Breakfast · Hershey & Derry Township

    The Hershey Pantry

    Tiny scratch kitchen on Chocolate Avenue voted Central Pennsylvania's best breakfast by Harrisburg Magazine readers for some two decades running; no reservations, so lines form early. Order: Stuffed French toast, baked oatmeal and giant cinnamon rolls from the scratch bakery.

    801 E Chocolate Ave, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Tasting Table, Central Penn Business Journal, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  4. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Hershey & Derry Township

    Tröegs Independent Brewing

    The Trogner brothers' brewery, moved from Harrisburg to a 90,000-sq-ft Hershey plant in 2011; its one-hour tour (with tastings) was voted the No. 1 brewery tour in America by USA Today readers. Big tasting room and beer garden with a full view of the brewhouse. Order: Troegenator Double Bock, Perpetual IPA and the cult holiday Mad Elf, on tap where they're brewed.

    200 Hersheypark Dr, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg, USA Today 10Best

  5. Must see · Hershey & Derry Township

    Hersheypark

    Milton Hershey's 1906 employee picnic ground grown into one of the country's great amusement parks — 15 roller coasters including Candymonium, plus ZooAmerica and The Boardwalk water park — with the scent of the chocolate plant drifting over the midway.

    Look for ICON

    100 W Hersheypark Dr, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney)

  6. Must see · Hershey & Derry Township

    Hershey's Chocolate World

    The Hershey Company's free visitor center: a simulated factory-tour ride from cocoa bean to wrapped bar (with a sample), plus paid extras — design-your-own candy bar, the HERSHEY'S Unwrapped tasting show — and the world's largest Hershey store.

    Look for FACT

    101 Chocolate World Way, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  7. Must see · Chocolate, Candy & Ice Cream · Hershey & Derry Township

    The Jigger Shop

    Mount Gretna's seasonal ice-cream parlor, a Chautauqua tradition since 1895; its spring opening day is local news. Order: Sundaes and hand-dipped ice cream at Mount Gretna's 1895 parlor.

    202 Gettysburg Ave, Mount Gretna, PA 17064

    Recommended by LebTown, Spotlight PA

  8. Must see · Italian & Pizza · Hershey & Derry Township

    Fenicci's of Hershey

    Hershey's oldest free-standing restaurant (since 1935) and the first in town to serve pizza (1947) — old family sauce recipes on Chocolate Avenue. Order: House meatballs, lasagna and the upside-down pizza.

    102 W Chocolate Ave, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  9. Worth the detour · Hershey & Derry Township

    ZooAmerica North American Wildlife Park

    An 11-acre walk-through zoo of 200 animals from five regions of North America — black bears, wolves, bald eagles — begun in 1910 as Milton Hershey's private animal collection; entry included with Hersheypark.

    Look for FAM

    30 Park Ave, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit PA (state tourism office), Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  10. Worth the detour · Hershey & Derry Township

    Mount Gretna

    A wooded 1890s Chautauqua and camp-meeting colony of tiny cottages on a lake between Hershey and Lancaster — summer theater at the Gretna Playhouse, a famous outdoor art show, music in the Tabernacle, and the 1895 Jigger Shop.

    Look for ODD

    Mount Gretna, PA 17064

    Recommended by Spotlight PA, Washingtonian, Visit Lebanon Valley

  11. Worth the detour · Hershey & Derry Township

    Union Canal Tunnel Park

    The oldest existing transportation tunnel in the United States: 729 feet hand-cut through slate in 1825–27 for the Union Canal linking Middletown to Reading; walk through it, or ride summer boat tours, off the Lebanon Valley Rail Trail.

    Look for HIST

    Union Canal Tunnel Park, Lebanon, PA 17046

    Recommended by Asce, abc27 WHTM (Harrisburg), Lebanon County Historical Society

  12. Worth the detour · Hershey & Derry Township

    The Hotel Hershey

    Milton Hershey's Depression-era (1933) Mediterranean-style grand hotel on Pat's Hill above the chocolate factory — famous for its circular dining room, built so no guest would be seated in a corner ('if you don't tip well, they put you in a corner'). A Historic Hotels of America member.

    Look for HIST

    100 Hotel Rd, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Hershey Community Archives, Historic Hotels of America (National Trust), Saharchipedia

  13. Worth the detour · Italian & Pizza · Hershey & Derry Township

    Alfred's Victorian

    Pellegrini family's restaurant in a restored brownstone mansion in Middletown, serving since 1970 — reviewed by WITF's Phantom Diner. Order: Italian classics and seafood, or Saturday Victorian tea.

    Look for Dinner Fri–Sat; Saturday luncheon/tea.

    38 N Union St, Middletown, PA 17057

    Recommended by Witf (Harrisburg public media — NPR/PBS), PA Eats, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  14. Worth the detour · American & New American · Hershey & Derry Township

    Mount Gretna Hideaway

    Rustic Mount Gretna tavern with a forest-view deck; its lobster bisque placed second in the Lebanon Valley Food Critics' soup contest. Order: Lobster bisque (#2 in LebTown's Soup Wars) and wings on the deck.

    40 Boulevard Ave, Mount Gretna, PA 17064

    Recommended by LebTown, Visit PA (state tourism office), Visit Lebanon Valley

  15. Worth the detour · Hershey & Derry Township

    Hershey Gardens & Butterfly Atrium

    Milton Hershey's 1937 rose garden grown to 23 acres of themed gardens on the hill by The Hotel Hershey, plus one of the country's few indoor tropical butterfly atriums, with 500-plus butterflies year-round.

    Look for PARK

    170 Hotel Rd, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Penn State Extension, Central Penn Business Journal

  16. Worth the detour · Hershey & Derry Township

    AACA Museum

    A Smithsonian affiliate with three floors of cars, buses and motorcycles from the 1890s to the 1980s set in period dioramas, plus the Tucker automobile collection — Hershey is the antique-car world's capital each October.

    Look for MUS

    161 Museum Dr, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Wikipedia, PA Bucket List

  17. Worth the detour · Hershey & Derry Township

    Cornwall Iron Furnace

    A complete charcoal-era ironworks — furnace stack, blast machinery and ironmaster's village — that made iron from 1742 to 1883, including cannon for the Revolution; a PHMC-run National Historic Landmark.

    Look for HIST

    Rexmont Rd & Boyd St, Cornwall, PA 17016

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Inventiontech

  18. Worth the detour · American & New American · Hershey & Derry Township

    The Chocolate Avenue Grill

    Unpretentious, broad-menu grill in downtown Hershey that a local guide and the visitor bureau both send people to — burgers to lobster, with chocolate desserts to finish. Order: Burgers, Reubens and chocolate desserts.

    114 W Chocolate Ave, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  19. Worth the detour · Bakeries, Shoofly & Whoopie Pies · Hershey & Derry Township

    Desserts Etc.

    The Hershey Pantry's sister bakery-café on East Chocolate Avenue, one of Tasting Table's six must-try Chocolate Avenue eateries. Order: Cupcakes, cookies and quiche from the Pantry's bakery.

    840 E Chocolate Ave, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Tasting Table, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg

  20. Deep cut · American & New American · Hershey & Derry Township

    Hershey Social Restaurant + Bar

    Downtown Hershey's newest bar-restaurant (replacing Houlihan's, 2026) with darts and trivia — on Tasting Table's Chocolate Avenue list. Order: Smash burgers, signature-sauce wings and cocktails.

    27 W Chocolate Ave, Hershey, PA 17033

    Recommended by Tasting Table, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg, FOX43 WPMT (York)

Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley 14

Boiling Springs, Shippensburg

  1. Must see · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    Carlisle Fairgrounds (Carlisle Events car shows)

    Home of Carlisle Events and the largest collector-car shows in the country — Spring and Fall Carlisle swap meets with 8,000-plus vendor spaces and a 2,000-car corral, plus the Ford, GM, Chrysler, Truck, Import and Corvette Nationals through the summer.

    Look for ODD

    1000 Bryn Mawr Rd, Carlisle, PA 17013

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit Cumberland Valley, Central Penn Business Journal, Old Cars Weekly

  2. Must see · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    Pine Grove Furnace State Park

    A 696-acre DCNR park around the ruins of an 18th-century iron furnace in the Mountain Creek valley — the Appalachian Trail's symbolic halfway point, with Fuller and Laurel lakes for swimming and paddling, the AT Museum and the half-gallon ice cream challenge store.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    1100 Pine Grove Rd, Gardners, PA 17324

    Recommended by Wikipedia, PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, Visit Cumberland Valley

  3. Must see · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    U.S. Army Heritage and Education Center

    The Army's own history museum beside the Army War College: the Soldier Experience Gallery runs from the Revolution to Afghanistan, and the outdoor Army Heritage Trail has a WWI trench, Civil War cabins and Cold War vehicles. Free.

    Look for MUS

    950 Soldiers Dr, Carlisle, PA 17013

    Recommended by American Battlefield Trust, Stars and Stripes

  4. Must see · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    Appalachian Trail Museum

    The first museum devoted to hiking, in a 200-year-old gristmill at Pine Grove Furnace State Park — near the AT's symbolic halfway point, where thru-hikers sign in and celebrate.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    1120 Pine Grove Rd, Gardners, PA 17324

    Recommended by Spotlight PA, Visit Cumberland Valley

  5. Must see · Diners & Breakfast · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    Hamilton Restaurant

    Downtown Carlisle diner on the old 'Greek Row,' widely regarded as the town's oldest continuously operating restaurant; Greek immigrant Charles Kollas created the Hot-Chee Dog here in 1938, and it now has its own historical marker. Winner of the 2023 Cumberland Valley Meal Madness bracket. Order: The Hot-Chee Dog — grilled dog, American cheese, house chili, yellow mustard and diced onions, served since 1938.

    55 W High St, Carlisle, PA 17013

    Recommended by Amazing America (Sinclair Broadcast Group), Visit Cumberland Valley

  6. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    Desperate Times Brewery

    Award-winning Carlisle brewery (US Open Beer Championship and Great American Beer Festival medals) — 12 taps, full kitchen and outdoor biergarten on the Cumberland Valley Beer Trail. Order: Prohibition-themed medal-winning beers with a full menu in the biergarten.

    1201 Carlisle Springs Rd, Carlisle, PA 17013

    Recommended by Visit Cumberland Valley, The Sentinel (Carlisle) / cumberlink.com

  7. Worth the detour · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    Carlisle Indian School Cemetery

    The Carlisle Barracks post cemetery where at least 180 Native American students of the Carlisle Indian Industrial School (1879–1918), the federal boarding school that became the model for forced assimilation, are buried; the Army has returned dozens of children's remains to their tribes since 2017. A place of reflection, on an active Army post.

    Look for HIST

    530 E North St, Carlisle, PA 17013

    Recommended by Georgia Public Broadcasting (PBS/NPR member), U.S. Army War College (Carlisle Barracks), Dickinson

  8. Worth the detour · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    Kings Gap Environmental Education Center

    A 2,531-acre DCNR forest on South Mountain crowned by the 32-room Italian-villa Cameron-Masland Mansion, with 25-plus miles of trails and a mountaintop view over the Cumberland Valley.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    500 Kings Gap Rd, Carlisle, PA 17015

    Recommended by PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, Dickinson, PA Bucket List

  9. Worth the detour · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    Dickinson College & The Trout Gallery

    Chartered in 1783 by Benjamin Rush — the first college founded after U.S. independence; its Trout Gallery art museum hosts rotating exhibits.

    Look for HIST

    240 W High St, Carlisle, PA 17013

    Recommended by Visit Cumberland Valley, Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney)

  13. Deep cut · American & New American · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

  14. Deep cut · Coffee & Cafés · Carlisle & the Cumberland Valley

    Caffe 101

York & York County 23

Hanover, the factory-tour trail

  1. Must see · Farms, Orchards & U-Pick · York & York County

    Brown's Orchards & Farm Market

    Family farm market since 1948 — 41,000 trees, a 29,000-sq-ft market with full bakery, café and hand-dipped Hershey's ice cream; ranked among the nation's best apple orchards (abc27). Order: Apple dumplings, cider donuts, award-winning cider and fresh pies.

    8892 Susquehanna Trail S, Loganville, PA 17342

    Recommended by Witf (Harrisburg public media — NPR/PBS), Visit PA (state tourism office), abc27 WHTM (Harrisburg), Explore York (York County CVB)

  2. Must see · York & York County

    Colonial Complex & Colonial Courthouse (York County History Center)

    Where the Continental Congress, fleeing British-occupied Philadelphia, met in the winter of 1777–78 and adopted the Articles of Confederation — making York, by local reckoning, America's first capital. A bicentennial replica courthouse holds an original printing of the Articles, beside the 1741 Golden Plough Tavern and the General Gates House.

    Look for HIST

    157 W Market St, York, PA 17401

    Recommended by National Park Service, Visit PA (state tourism office), Wikipedia

  3. Must see · York & York County

    Haines Shoe House

    A 25-foot-tall, 48-foot-long house shaped like a work boot, built in 1948 by 'Shoe Wizard' Mahlon Haines to advertise his shoe stores — a Route 30 roadside icon with a PA historical marker; tours and ice cream in season.

    Look for ODD

    197 Shoe House Rd, York, PA 17406

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Atlas Obscura, Central Penn Business Journal

  4. Must see · Italian & Pizza · York & York County

    Tutoni's

    Downtown York's Old-World Italian dining room — house-made pasta, soups and sauces, a Wine Spectator Award of Excellence (2025) and a speakeasy tapas bar upstairs. Order: Made-from-scratch pasta (short-rib gnocchi) and the upstairs speakeasy tapas bar.

    108 N George St, York, PA 17401

    Recommended by PA Eats, Wine Spectator Restaurant Awards, York Daily Record

  5. Must see · American & New American · York & York County

    John Wright Restaurant

    Riverside restaurant in an old Wrightsville warehouse across from Columbia — 60–70% of ingredients from local farms, with a patio over the Susquehanna. Order: Farm-sourced comfort food and house-made ice cream on the Susquehanna patio.

    234 N Front St, Wrightsville, PA 17368

    Recommended by PA Eats, Lancasteronline / LNP, Central Penn Business Journal

  6. Must see · Markets · York & York County

    Central Market York

    Downtown York's 1888 John Dempwolf market house, a Romanesque Revival landmark on the National Register since 1978, in continuous operation since it opened; 50-plus vendors, some trading here for more than 70 years. Order: Generations-old stands — Henry's Ham, J. L. Miller Meats, Hartman's Fruit Farm — plus a food-hall's worth of lunch counters.

    34 W Philadelphia St, York, PA 17401

    Recommended by Visit PA (state tourism office), Clio (Marshall University)

  7. Must see · Pretzels, Chips & Snack Factories · York & York County

    Utz Snacks Factory Tour & Outlet

    The glass-walled observation gallery above Utz's Hanover plant shows potatoes going from truck to fryer to bag, then deposits you in the factory outlet — the signature stop in the 'Snack Food Capital of the World.' Order: Fresh-off-the-line Utz potato chips after the free self-guided Chip Trip.

    900 High St, Hanover, PA 17331

    Recommended by NPR (The Salt), Northern Virginia Magazine

  8. Must see · Asian · York & York County

    Viet Thai Cafe

    Two-decade family kitchen in a York strip mall cooking Thai, Laotian and Vietnamese food — one of only three Pennsylvania restaurants on USA Today's 2024 Restaurants of the Year list. Order: Pho, house noodle soup and beef massaman curry.

    Look for Closed Sundays.

    2535 E Market St, York, PA 17402

    Recommended by The Philadelphia Inquirer, York Daily Record

  9. Must see · Asian · York & York County

    Hamir's Indian Fusion

    Self-taught chef's downtown York dining room — named to USA Today's Restaurants of the Year list, the York Daily Record's pick for York's best. Order: Signature curries with fusion twists and plated desserts.

    24 S George St, York, PA 17401

    Recommended by USA Today 10Best, York Daily Record

  10. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · York & York County

    Wyndridge Farm

    Working farm south of York with a cidery, brewery and seasonal farm-sourced restaurant — brick-oven pizzas and house-made ice cream. Order: Hard ciders, house beer and brick-oven pizza on the farm.

    885 S Pleasant Ave, Dallastown, PA 17313

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), PA Eats

  11. Must see · Chocolate, Candy & Ice Cream · York & York County

    Perrydell Farm Dairy

    Century family dairy farm that bottles its own hormone-free milk and churns it into ice cream at the farm store — 30 flavours in the case at a time. Order: Farm-made ice cream from its own herd's milk (250 rotating flavours).

    90 Indian Rock Dam Rd, York, PA 17403

    Recommended by PA Eats, FOX43 WPMT (York)

  12. Worth the detour · York & York County

    Codorus State Park & Lake Marburg

    3,500-acre DCNR park around 1,275-acre Lake Marburg — the reservoir that drowned the village of Marburg in 1966 — with kayaking, sailing, fishing and trails near Hanover.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    2600 Smith Station Rd, Hanover, PA 17331

    Recommended by Wikipedia, PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, Mid-Atlantic Day Trips

  13. Worth the detour · York & York County

    York County Heritage Rail Trail

    A 21-mile National Recreation Trail on the Northern Central Railway corridor from downtown York to the Mason–Dixon line, passing Hanover Junction station, where Lincoln changed trains on the way to deliver the Gettysburg Address.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    Trailhead at Colonial Courthouse, W Market St, York, PA 17401

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Witf (Harrisburg public media — NPR/PBS), Bay Journal

  14. Worth the detour · York & York County

    Samuel S. Lewis State Park (Mount Pisgah)

    An 85-acre hilltop park on 885-foot Mount Pisgah near Wrightsville, with a sweeping overlook of the Susquehanna winding toward the Chesapeake — a favorite kite-flying and stargazing spot.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    6000 Mount Pisgah Rd, York, PA 17406

    Recommended by Wikipedia, PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, Susquehanna Greenway Partnership

  15. Worth the detour · York & York County

    Indian Steps Museum

    Judge John Vandersloot's 1908–12 Arts-and-Crafts cabin above the Susquehanna, built as a memorial and museum to Native American culture, with thousands of artifacts set into its walls.

    Look for MUS

    205 Indian Steps Rd, Airville, PA 17302

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Visit PA (state tourism office), Atlas Obscura

  16. Worth the detour · York & York County

    Columbia–Wrightsville Bridge & Zimmerman Center

    Where Union militia burned the mile-long covered bridge on June 28, 1863 to stop Confederates crossing the Susquehanna — the farthest east Lee's army reached. Today's 1930 concrete-arch bridge is an ASCE landmark; the riverside Zimmerman Center is the visitor station for the Captain John Smith Chesapeake National Historic Trail.

    Look for CIVIL

    Zimmerman Center, 1706 Long Level Rd, Wrightsville, PA 17368

    Recommended by Asce, National Park Service, PA Eats

  17. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · York & York County

    Collusion Tap Works

    Brewery-restaurant hidden on a back alley in York's Royal Square, run by the Barnes family; eclectic, ever-changing tap list. Order: Rotating farmhouse ales and stouts (650+ recipes since 2016).

    105 S Howard St, York, PA 17401

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), Lancasteronline / LNP, The York Dispatch

  18. Worth the detour · York & York County

    Ma & Pa Railroad Heritage Village

    The preserved railroad hamlet of Muddy Creek Forks on the old Maryland & Pennsylvania ('Ma & Pa') line — general store, mill and grain elevator, with seasonal motor-car and train rides through the Muddy Creek valley.

    Look for RAIL

    Muddy Creek Forks, Airville, PA 17302

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Lancaster County Magazine

  19. Worth the detour · York & York County

    Hanover Junction Railroad Station

    The restored junction depot on the Heritage Rail Trail where Lincoln changed trains en route to deliver the Gettysburg Address in November 1863; small museum of Civil War images and station history.

    Look for CIVIL

    PA Route 616, Hanover Junction (North Codorus Twp), PA 17362

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Witf (Harrisburg public media — NPR/PBS)

  20. Worth the detour · Pretzels, Chips & Snack Factories · York & York County

    Martin's Potato Chips

    York County family chipmaker in Thomasville since the 1940s; free 45-minute tours run Tuesday mornings by reservation — pair it with Utz and Snyder's in nearby Hanover for the full 'Snack Food Capital' circuit. Order: Kettle-style Martin's potato chips, fresh from the free Tuesday factory tour.

    5847 Lincoln Hwy W, Thomasville, PA 17364

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), PA Eats

  21. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · York & York County

    Mudhook Brewing Company

    Downtown York brewpub that Uncovering PA singles out as much for its food as its beer; on Explore York's Beer Lovers Guide. Order: House beers with a full kitchen menu.

    34 N Cherry Ln, York, PA 17401

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), Explore York (York County CVB)

  22. Deep cut · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · York & York County

    Liquid Hero Brewery

    York craft brewery with superhero-named beers, on Explore York's Beer Lovers Guide and Uncovering PA's downtown itinerary. Order: Comic-book-themed craft beers.

    50 E North St, York, PA 17401

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), Explore York (York County CVB), FOX43 WPMT (York)

  23. Deep cut · York & York County

    Gifford Pinchot State Park

    2,338-acre northern York County park around 340-acre Pinchot Lake — hiking, boating and disc golf.

    Look for PARK

    2200 Rosstown Rd, Lewisberry, PA 17339

    Recommended by PA DCNR — Pennsylvania State Parks, Explore York (York County CVB)

Lancaster city 29

Central Market, Penn Square, the Gallery Row

  1. Must see · Lancaster city

    Wheatland (James Buchanan House)

    The 1828 Federal-style home of James Buchanan, the 15th president, who ran his 1856 campaign from its library; guided tours from the adjacent LancasterHistory campus.

    Look for HIST

    1120 Marietta Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), National Park Service

  2. Must see · Lancaster city

    Fulton Theatre

    Built in 1852 on the foundations of the jail where the Conestoga were massacred in 1763, the 'Grand Old Lady of Prince Street' is among the oldest continuously operating theaters in the US and a National Historic Landmark; Mark Twain lectured here.

    Look for HIST

    12 N Prince St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Wikipedia, LancasterHistory, LancasterPA.com

  3. Must see · Markets · Lancaster city

    Lancaster Central Market

    Recognized as the oldest continuously operating public farmers market in the US (est. 1730), in an 1889 Romanesque Revival market house off Penn Square. 60-plus standholders; open Tue, Fri and Sat mornings only — go early. Order: Stall-hop the PA Dutch canon — shoofly and whoopie pies, sweet bologna, chow-chow — plus pierogi, empanadas and soul food.

    23 N Market St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), Tasting Table, LancasterPA.com

  4. Must see · American & New American · Lancaster city

    Horse Inn

    Lancaster city's oldest continuously operating restaurant: a mid-1800s carriage house whose loft became a 1920s speakeasy. Horse stalls are dining nooks, wagon wheels the chandeliers, and the original entrance still hides down an unnamed alley. Order: Tenderloin tips on toast — the Shaub family's Prohibition-era speakeasy dish, still on the menu.

    540 E Fulton St, Lancaster, PA 17602

    Recommended by Islands, Lancaster County Magazine, Uncharted Lancaster

  5. Must see · American & New American · Lancaster city

    Passerine

    French-inspired New American spot (opened 2024) cooking the county's farm bounty; named to the New York Times' 50 favorite restaurants in America and Craig LaBan's 2026 Lancaster list. Order: Seasonal small plates — seared scallops with summer corn, the 25-layer zucchini–goat ricotta crêpe cake.

    114 N Prince St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by The New York Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer, Lancaster County Magazine

  6. Must see · Mexican, Puerto Rican & Latin · Lancaster city

    Chellas Arepa Kitchen

    Food truck turned downtown restaurant (2025) — Lancaster County Magazine's #1 food truck, then #1 new restaurant, and on Craig LaBan's 2026 Lancaster list. Order: Arepas and Peruvian–Venezuelan plates.

    325 N Queen St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by The Philadelphia Inquirer, Lancaster County Magazine, Lancasteronline / LNP

  7. Must see · Asian · Lancaster city

    Issei Noodle & Hi-Fi Izakaya

    Donna and André Pham's family noodle house (Japanese, Thai and Laotian roots) — André trained in Tokyo and makes noodles in-house on an imported machine; moved in 2024 to a bigger Orange Street space with the attached Hi-Fi Izakaya bar. LNP calls its gyoza the best in the county. Order: House-made ramen noodles, handmade gyoza and mochi doughnuts.

    W Orange St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by The Philadelphia Inquirer, Lancasteronline / LNP, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB)

  8. Must see · Coffee & Cafés · Lancaster city

    Passenger Coffee

    Lancaster roaster named Pennsylvania's best coffee shop by Food & Wine in 2018, 2019 and 2022 — the Inquirer's first stop on a Lancaster weekend. Order: Pour-overs and espresso from its own roastery.

    7 W King St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Lancasteronline / LNP, The Philadelphia Inquirer, Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney)

  9. Must see · American & New American · Lancaster city

    The Belvedere Inn

    Victorian-mansion dining room voted #1 dinner restaurant in Lancaster County Magazine's Best of Lancaster 2025; on OpenTable's Top 100 romantic restaurants. Order: Fine dining downstairs, rooftop patio and piano bar.

    402 N Queen St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Lancaster County Magazine, Lancasteronline / LNP

  10. Must see · Markets · Lancaster city

    Southern Market

    The 1888 Southern Market building, reinvented in 2022 as a food hall of independent, internationally minded stalls a block from Penn Square. Order: International stalls — Latin, Moroccan, Vietnamese and more — under one 1888 roof.

    100 S Queen St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by The Philadelphia Inquirer, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB)

  11. Must see · Italian & Pizza · Lancaster city

    Luca

    Chef Nathan Flaim's acclaimed Italian restaurant, a 2026 James Beard Award finalist for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic — the city's highest national culinary honor in years. Order: Wood-fired Neapolitan-leaning pizzas and handmade pasta from local Lancaster County produce.

    436 W James St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation

  12. Worth the detour · Lancaster city

    Demuth Museum

    The home and studio of Precisionist painter Charles Demuth (1883–1935), with the world's largest Demuth collection, his mother's garden, and the family's 1770 tobacco shop next door — America's oldest.

    Look for MUS

    120 E King St, Lancaster, PA 17602

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Artistshomes, LancasterPA.com

  13. Worth the detour · Lancaster city

    Historic Rock Ford

    The 1794 Georgian mansion of Gen. Edward Hand, Washington's adjutant general, on the Conestoga River in Lancaster County Central Park — remarkably intact, with original woodwork and period furnishings.

    Look for HIST

    881 Rock Ford Rd, Lancaster, PA 17602

    Recommended by Wikipedia, LancasterPA.com, Clio (Marshall University)

  14. Worth the detour · American & New American · Lancaster city

    Cabalar Meat Co.

    Chef Steve and pastry chef Lianne Cabalar's whole-animal butcher shop and lunch counter (2018), breaking down local pasture-raised animals in front of you on North Queen Street. Order: Whole-animal-butcher burgers and sandwiches — Lancaster County Magazine readers' favorite burger.

    501 W Lemon St (West End Market), Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Lancaster County Magazine, PA Eats, Lancasteronline / LNP

  15. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Lancaster city

    Lancaster Brewing Company

    Opened in 1995 in the National Register-listed McGovern tobacco warehouse at Plum and Walnut — the first brewery to operate in Lancaster in some 40 years, in a county that brewed 7% of America's beer in 1810. Order: House beers from a brewery that has made 200-plus styles since 1995, with a full brewpub menu.

    302 N Plum St, Lancaster, PA 17602

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Lancaster County Magazine, Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney)

  16. Worth the detour · American & New American · Lancaster city

    Josephine's Downtown

    Old-Hollywood supper club (blue-velvet banquettes) cooking continental French-American food; on OpenTable's 2025 Top 100 Romantic Restaurants in America. Order: Seared scallops, duck breast and prime beef tenderloin.

    50 W Grant St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Lancasteronline / LNP, Lancaster County Magazine, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB)

  17. Worth the detour · Lancaster city

    Lancaster Science Factory

    Hands-on science center with 70-plus interactive exhibits aimed at kids 6 to 14 — build, test and tinker; a reliable rainy-day stop in the city.

    Look for FAM

    454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA 17602

    Recommended by LancasterPA.com, Central Penn Business Journal

  18. Worth the detour · Lancaster city

    North Museum of Nature and Science

    Franklin & Marshall-linked natural-science museum — 360,000 specimens, planetarium shows and a live-animal room on three floors.

    Look for MUS

    400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), Visit PA (state tourism office)

  19. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Lancaster city

    Spring House Brewing Company

    Lancaster's inventive brewery, best known for its dessert stouts and pumpkin ales; the taproom is just outside downtown with a second tasting room on West King Street. Order: Award-winning chocolate peanut-butter stout and the brewery's pumpkin ale.

    209 Hazel St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), Lancaster County Magazine

  20. Worth the detour · Italian & Pizza · Lancaster city

    Pizzeria LUCA

    Casual wood-fired pizza offshoot of James Beard-nominated LUCA — #2 pizza in Lancaster County Magazine's Best of Lancaster 2025 and on Craig LaBan's 2026 list.

  21. Worth the detour · Asian · Lancaster city

    Himalayan Curry & Grill

    Tiny downtown Nepalese–Indian locals' favourite (reserve — few tables), reviewed by LNP's IncognEATo. Order: Nepalese momos and curries.

    22 E Orange St, Lancaster, PA 17602

    Recommended by Lancasteronline / LNP, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB)

  22. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Lancaster city

    Proof

    Speakeasy-style cocktail bar down a metal stair below street level — stone walls, live jazz, and food LNP rates worth the trip on its own. Order: Craft cocktails and upscale small plates with live jazz.

    30 N Queen St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Lancasteronline / LNP, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB)

  23. Worth the detour · American & New American · Lancaster city

    Irish-rooted multi-level pub and music venue off Penn Square whose summer rooftop garden is a Lancaster institution; host of the VeloCity cocktail contest. Order: Pints and cocktails on the garden rooftop.

    24 E King St, Lancaster, PA 17602

    Recommended by Lancasteronline / LNP, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB)

    Annie Bailey's Irish Public House

    Downtown Irish pub with one of the city's best decks (Discover Lancaster) and an LNP readers' pick for cocktails — the Conway Social Club speakeasy hides behind a green unmarked door inside. Order: Irish pub fare on the deck; cocktails at the hidden Conway Social Club.

    28 E King St, Lancaster, PA 17602

  25. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Lancaster city

    Thistle Finch Distillery

    Lancaster's oldest operating distillery, in a historic tobacco warehouse — spirits from local grain, tasting room and the Burley Bar restaurant. Order: Straight Rye and Market Alley Gin; cocktails at the Burley Bar.

    417 W Grant St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), Lancasteronline / LNP

    216 Harrisburg Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Lancasteronline / LNP, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB)

  27. Deep cut · Lancaster city

    Holy Trinity Lutheran Church

    The oldest church still in use in Lancaster city (congregation 1729, built 1761–66); its Washington-era steeple was once the tallest point west of Philadelphia. Sanctuary tours with First Friday lectures.

    Look for HIST

    31 S Duke St, Lancaster, PA 17602

    Recommended by Lancasteronline / LNP, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), LancasterHistory

  28. Deep cut · Lancaster city

    Penn Medicine Park (Clipper Magazine Stadium)

    Home of the Lancaster Stormers since 2005 (renamed from Clipper Magazine Stadium in 2025) — fans' pick for best independent ballpark of the year.

    Look for FAM

    650 N Prince St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), Lancasteronline / LNP

  29. Deep cut · Coffee & Cafés · Lancaster city

    Prince Street Cafe

    15 N Prince St, Lancaster, PA 17603

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB)

Lancaster County Amish country 34

Intercourse, Bird-in-Hand, Strasburg, Ephrata, Lititz

  1. Must see · Lancaster County Amish country

    Landis Valley Village & Farm Museum

    A 100-acre living-history crossroads village of Pennsylvania German rural life, founded on the Landis brothers' collection; costumed interpreters, heirloom-seed gardens and 18th–19th-century trades.

    Look for HIST

    2451 Kissel Hill Rd, Lancaster, PA 17601

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), PA Heritage / Trails of History (PHMC)

  2. Must see · Lancaster County Amish country

    Chickies Rock Overlook

    A 1-mile out-and-back on an old trolley grade to a quartzite cliff 200 feet above the Susquehanna — the classic river panorama of Lancaster County, in a 400-acre county park.

    Look for OUTDOOR

    Chickies Rock County Park, PA-441, Columbia, PA 17512

    Recommended by Uncovering PA (Jim Cheney), Wikipedia, Susquehanna Greenway Partnership

  3. Must see · Lancaster County Amish country

    Middle Creek Wildlife Management Area

    A 6,000-acre Game Commission refuge on the Lancaster–Lebanon line where, each February–March, tens to hundreds of thousands of snow geese and tundra swans stop on their way back to the Arctic — one of the great wildlife spectacles in the East. Check the PGC migration update before you go.

    Look for PARK

    100 Museum Rd, Stevens, PA 17578

    Recommended by Pagov, Witf (Harrisburg public media — NPR/PBS), The Philadelphia Inquirer

  4. Must see · Lancaster County Amish country

    Sight & Sound Theatres

    The 2,000-seat home of Bible epics staged on a 300-foot wraparound stage with four-story sets, live animals and animatronics — Lancaster County's biggest draw by attendance, with more than a million visitors a year across its two theaters.

    Look for FAM

    300 Hartman Bridge Rd, Ronks, PA 17572

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Religion News Service, Live Design

  5. Must see · Lancaster County Amish country

    Downtown Lititz & Moravian Church Square

    Budget Travel readers' 'Coolest Small Town in America' (2013): a 1756 Moravian settlement whose Church Square ensemble — the white-belfried church, Brothers' and Sisters' Houses, God's Acre cemetery — anchors a Main Street of cafés and shops, plus Lititz Springs Park and the Sturgis pretzel bakery.

    Look for HIST

    8 Church Square, Lititz, PA 17543

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Central Penn Business Journal, Fox News Travel

  6. Must see · Bakeries, Shoofly & Whoopie Pies · Lancaster County Amish country

    Dutch Haven Shoo-Fly Pie Bakery

    Lancaster County's first tourist attraction (1946) and 'the place that made shoo-fly pie famous' — it began serving the molasses-and-crumb pie to Route 30 travelers and shipping it nationwide in the 1950s; TIME once called it America's best. Also a sprawling Amish-country gift shop under the landmark windmill. Order: Wet-bottom shoofly pie from the original 1946 recipe, served warm with whipped cream.

    2857A Lincoln Hwy E, Ronks, PA 17572

    Recommended by The Philadelphia Inquirer, Frommer's, LancasterPA.com

  7. Must see · Pennsylvania Dutch & Smorgasbords · Lancaster County Amish country

    Shady Maple Smorgasbord

    The largest buffet in North America: 200 feet of Pennsylvania Dutch cooking serving some 1.2 million diners a year, voted best buffet in the US by USA Today 10Best readers (2024). A pilgrimage in itself — go hungry, go early. Order: PA Dutch smorgasbord — chicken pot pie, schnitz un knepp, carved ham, buttered noodles and a dessert bar of shoofly and whoopie pies.

    129 Toddy Dr, East Earl, PA 17519

    Recommended by Wikipedia, WFMZ-TV 69 News, Amish America (Erik Wesner)

  8. Must see · Pennsylvania Dutch & Smorgasbords · Lancaster County Amish country

    Miller's Smorgasbord

    A Lancaster County institution since 1929, when it began as a chicken-and-waffles stop for Route 30 motorists; placed third in USA Today 10Best's readers' poll for best buffet. The more traditional, sit-and-linger smorgasbord counterpart to Shady Maple's scale. Order: Chicken & waffles (the dish that started it in 1929) and the traditional PA Dutch smorgasbord with shoofly pie.

    2811 Lincoln Hwy E, Ronks, PA 17572

    Recommended by USA Today 10Best, Amish America (Erik Wesner), LancasterPA.com

  9. Must see · Pretzels, Chips & Snack Factories · Lancaster County Amish country

    Julius Sturgis Pretzel Bakery

    America's first commercial pretzel bakery, opened in 1861 in an 18th-century Lititz house; the original ovens are still here and every tour ends with you twisting your own. The birthplace of the hard pretzel in the US. Order: Hand-twisted soft and hard pretzels — and a hands-on twisting lesson.

    219 E Main St, Lititz, PA 17543

    Recommended by Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), 6abc Action News (wpvi, Philadelphia Abc O&O), Chowhound

  10. Must see · Bakeries, Shoofly & Whoopie Pies · Lancaster County Amish country

    Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe

    The Smucker family's scratch bakery in the village of Bird-in-Hand; its shoofly pie (a light-syrup, never-bitter take on the molasses classic) starred in Al Roker's 'Family Style' episode on the history of American pie. Whoopie-pie samplers by the dozen. Order: Grandma Smucker's wet-bottom shoofly pie and jumbo whoopie pies, baked from scratch.

    2715 Old Philadelphia Pike, Bird-in-Hand, PA 17505

    Recommended by Mashed, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), Frommer's

  11. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Lancaster County Amish country

    Bube's Brewery & Catacombs

    Alois Bube's 1876 brewery in Mount Joy — on the National Register and believed to be the only intact 19th-century lager-era brewery in the US; eat in the stone aging cellars, the biergarten or the Victorian hotel bar. Order: House-brewed beer and fine dining 43 feet underground in the lager-aging Catacombs.

    102 N Market St, Mount Joy, PA 17552

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Chowhound, Witf (Harrisburg public media — NPR/PBS)

  12. Must see · Pennsylvania Dutch & Smorgasbords · Lancaster County Amish country

    Hershey Farm Restaurant

    Strasburg-area PA Dutch smorgasbord and bakery, home of Lancaster's Whoopie Pie Festival; its whoopie pies topped LNP's blind taste test of county favorites. Order: Whoopie pies from the on-site bakery (top of LNP's county taste test) and the Grand Smorgasbord.

    240 Hartman Bridge Rd, Ronks, PA 17572

    Recommended by Lancasteronline / LNP, Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), Central Penn Business Journal

  13. Must see · Italian & Pizza · Lancaster County Amish country

    Cavolo Pizzeria Bar

    Chef Max Fanton's wood-fired pizzeria bar off Lititz's square (2024), already on Craig LaBan's 2026 list of Lancaster County's best. Order: Wood-fired pizzas and small plates with Italian wines.

    54 N Broad St, Lititz, PA 17543

    Recommended by The Philadelphia Inquirer, Lancasteronline / LNP, Lancaster County Magazine

  14. Must see · Pennsylvania Dutch & Smorgasbords · Lancaster County Amish country

    Plain & Fancy Farm

    Lancaster County's original family-style restaurant: big bowls passed round the table like at an Amish gathering. Order: Amish Farm Feast — fried chicken, PA Dutch chicken pot pie with homemade noodles, chow-chow, pepper cabbage.

    3121 Old Philadelphia Pike, Bird-in-Hand, PA 17505

    Recommended by Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), Amish America (Erik Wesner), Lancasteronline / LNP

  15. Must see · Lancaster County Amish country

    Strasburg Rail Road

    America's oldest continuously operating short-line railroad (chartered 1832): steam trains pull restored wooden coaches 45 minutes through Amish farmland to Paradise and back — the classic Lancaster County ride.

    Look for RAIL

    301 Gap Rd, Ronks, PA 17572

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Railfan Guides

  16. Must see · Lancaster County Amish country

    Railroad Museum of Pennsylvania

    The Commonwealth's railroad museum, across the road from the Strasburg Rail Road: more than 100 historic locomotives and cars, many from the Pennsylvania Railroad, under one vast roof.

    Look for RAIL

    300 Gap Rd, Ronks, PA 17572

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Railfan Guides

  17. Must see · Lancaster County Amish country

    Ephrata Cloister

    The medieval-looking 1730s timber buildings of Conrad Beissel's celibate German Seventh Day Baptist community — famous for its a cappella music, Fraktur calligraphy and printing press. Now a PHMC historic site and National Historic Landmark.

    Look for HIST

    632 W Main St, Ephrata, PA 17522

    Recommended by Wikipedia, PA Historical & Museum Commission

  18. Must see · Markets · Lancaster County Amish country

    Green Dragon Farmers Market & Auction

    A 60-acre Friday institution since 1932 — one of the largest and oldest farmers markets on the East Coast, with 400-plus vendors, a livestock and hay auction, and Amish and Mennonite stands. Voted the No. 2 farmers market in the US by USA Today readers (2021). Order: Friday-only feast: PA Dutch baked goods, sweet bologna and fresh-cut fries across 400 stands and an auction.

    955 N State St, Ephrata, PA 17522

    Recommended by Discover Lancaster (Lancaster County CVB), LancasterPA.com

    Stoll & Wolfe Distillery

    Revival of Lancaster County rye distilling, founded 2016 with Dick Stoll, last distiller of the old Michter's plant; tasting room a block off Main Street, Lititz. On Craig LaBan's 2026 Lancaster list. Order: Pennsylvania rye whiskey (Wine Enthusiast 94 — the highest-scoring PA whiskey).

    35 N Cedar St, Lititz, PA 17543

    Recommended by The Philadelphia Inquirer, Central Penn Business Journal

Gettysburg & Adams County 21

the day-trip edge

  1. Must see · Chocolate, Candy & Ice Cream · Gettysburg & Adams County

    Mr. G's Ice Cream

    Sixteen flavours made on the premises in the 1819 Twin Sycamores House on Baltimore Street — the town's classic after-battlefield scoop. Order: Homemade ice cream — chocolate peanut butter soft-serve sundae, butter pecan, root beer floats.

    404 Baltimore St, Gettysburg, PA 17325

    Recommended by Destination Gettysburg (Adams County CVB), TravelAwaits, PA Eats, Gettysburg Times

  2. Must see · Gettysburg & Adams County

    Little Round Top

    The rocky hill whose defense by the 20th Maine and others on July 2, 1863 anchored the Union left; reopened in June 2024 after a $12.9M rehabilitation restoring its 1863 look, with new trails and the best view over the Valley of Death and Devil's Den.

    Look for CIVIL

    Sykes Ave, Gettysburg National Military Park, PA 17325

    Recommended by National Park Service, Wikipedia, Emerging Civil War

  3. Must see · Gettysburg & Adams County

    Seminary Ridge Museum

    In 1832 Schmucker Hall of the Lutheran seminary, whose cupola Gen. John Buford used to watch the Confederates arrive on July 1, 1863; the museum covers the first day's fight, the building's use as a field hospital, and faith and freedom in the war — with guided cupola climbs.

    Look for CIVIL

    111 Seminary Ridge, Gettysburg, PA 17325

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Central Penn Business Journal, Evangelical Lutheran Church in America

  4. Must see · American & New American · Gettysburg & Adams County

    Dobbin House Tavern

    Gettysburg's oldest building (1776), Rev. Alexander Dobbin's home and later an Underground Railroad station, now a National Register-listed restaurant: candlelit fine dining upstairs, the cellar Springhouse Tavern with its springs and fireplaces below. Order: Colonial fare by candlelight — French onion soup in an iron kettle in the Springhouse Tavern.

    89 Steinwehr Ave, Gettysburg, PA 17325

    Recommended by Destination Gettysburg (Adams County CVB), Tasting Table, Blue & Gray Education Society

  5. Must see · Gettysburg & Adams County

    Gettysburg National Military Park Museum & Visitor Center

    Start here: the NPS museum, the film 'A New Birth of Freedom,' and Paul Philippoteaux's 1884 Gettysburg Cyclorama — a 377-foot painting-in-the-round of Pickett's Charge. Book a Licensed Battlefield Guide for the 6,000-acre field outside.

    Look for ICON

    1195 Baltimore Pike, Gettysburg, PA 17325

    Recommended by National Park Service, Wikipedia

  6. Must see · Gettysburg & Adams County

    Gettysburg National Cemetery (Soldiers' National Cemetery)

    Where Lincoln delivered the Gettysburg Address at its dedication on November 19, 1863; the semicircular rows of Union dead radiate around the Soldiers' National Monument. Evidence suggests the speakers' platform actually stood just over the fence in Evergreen Cemetery.

    Look for ICON

    97 Taneytown Rd, Gettysburg, PA 17325

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Hallowedground

  7. Must see · Gettysburg & Adams County

    High Water Mark & the Angle (Pickett's Charge)

    The copse of trees and stone wall on Cemetery Ridge where Pickett's Charge broke on July 3, 1863 — the deepest Confederate penetration of the Union line, marked by the 1892 High Water Mark of the Rebellion monument. Walk the mile across the open field from the Virginia Memorial to feel the scale.

    Look for CIVIL

    Hancock Ave, Cemetery Ridge, Gettysburg National Military Park, PA 17325

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Gettysburg Daily

  8. Must see · Pennsylvania Dutch & Smorgasbords · Gettysburg & Adams County

    Hickory Bridge Farm Restaurant

    A 160-year-old barn in the Adams County apple country west of Gettysburg serving made-from-scratch family-style farm dinners with a touch of PA Dutch. Order: Family-style fried chicken, baked ham, corn and apple crisp in the barn.

    Look for Dinners Fri–Sun; reservations.

    96 Hickory Bridge Rd, Orrtanna, PA 17353

    Recommended by Destination Gettysburg (Adams County CVB), TravelAwaits

  9. Worth the detour · Gettysburg & Adams County

    Devil's Den

    The boulder-strewn south end of Houck's Ridge, fought over on July 2, 1863 and later the lair of Confederate sharpshooters — and the scene of Alexander Gardner's famous staged 'sharpshooter' photograph. Scramble the rocks for the view up to Little Round Top.

    Look for CIVIL

    Crawford Ave, Gettysburg National Military Park, PA 17325

    Recommended by Wikipedia, National Park Service, American Battlefield Trust

  10. Worth the detour · Gettysburg & Adams County

    The 1858 depot where Abraham Lincoln arrived on November 18, 1863, the day before the Gettysburg Address; a field hospital during the battle, now a small NPS-owned museum run by the Gettysburg Foundation.

    Recommended by Wikipedia, Hallowedground, Blue & Gray Education Society

  11. Worth the detour · Gettysburg & Adams County

    Jennie Wade House

    Where 20-year-old Mary Virginia 'Jennie' Wade, baking bread for Union soldiers on July 3, 1863, was struck by a stray bullet — the only civilian killed in the battle. The bullet holes in the door remain; now a museum.

    Pennsylvania's first combined brewery-distillery, in the c.1848 brick-end barn of the W.H. Monfort Farm — one of the largest Confederate field hospitals after the battle (1,300+ wounded). Order: Rotating lagers, IPAs and stouts plus house spirits (Lincoln Lager).

77 sights and 94 places to eat across Harrisburg and the West Shore, Hershey, Carlisle, York, Lancaster and the Amish country of Lancaster County, with Gettysburg as the day-trip edge, each traceable to the source that named it. The food canon is Pennsylvania Dutch: shoofly pie, whoopie pies, square-noodle chicken pot pie, chow-chow, scrapple, Lititz soft pretzels, the York–Hanover snack belt, Hershey chocolate and the country’s oldest farmers’ markets.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. The canon is Pennsylvania Dutch: shoofly pie, whoopie pies, the square-noodle chicken pot pie, chow-chow, scrapple, Lititz soft pretzels (Julius Sturgis), the York–Hanover snack belt (Utz, Snyder’s), Hershey chocolate, family-style smorgasbords, and the standing markets (Lancaster Central Market, Harrisburg’s Broad Street Market). Amish farm stands often have no web presence; they still need two credible sources. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to credible sources — LancasterOnline/LNP, PennLive, the York Daily Record, WITF, Discover Lancaster, Visit Hershey & Harrisburg, Explore York, Destination Gettysburg, the National Park Service, PA DCNR, Smithsonian and official sites — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
